analysisMarkdown:
I like Commanders +3.5, but only as a lean. I have Indianapolis as a slight favorite in a one-score game, so I do not want the Colts laying this many points on the road after a messy start. This is not an automatic play. Three weeks is a tiny sample and I would not press the wager.

The displayed line is Commanders +3.5 at -108 against Colts -3.5, with the total at 47.5. Five books are on Washington +3.5 and four have already gone to +4. The three matters: a Colts win by exactly three cashes +3.5 and would only push if this were a 3, so the extra half-point is real value on this side. I would rather sit here than at +3, and +4 is where it starts to look like something I would actually bet.

Indianapolis was the stronger 2025 team at 8-9 while Washington went 5-12, and that longer body of work still outweighs three noisy weeks. Both clubs have allowed more than 30 points a game so far, and the Colts have already given up 24 explosive passes, which is the main reason I will not make them a bigger favorite. Washington has been efficient throwing the ball. Indianapolis is minus-5 in turnovers against a plus-2 Washington club, and that split is too extreme to treat as a true talent gap, so I keep the projected margin inside a field goal.

What keeps me from calling it a bet is last year's gap actually showing up on the field. If Indianapolis plays closer to that 8-9 club and Washington looks more like the 5-12 version, the Colts can win by a touchdown and +3.5 does not get there.

**Commanders +3.5: ~55% cover probability**
**Colts -3.5: ~45%**
**Fair-ish score: Colts 26, Commanders 25**
**Projected total: ~50.5**

So at the exact line I would choose Commanders +3.5. If it moved to +3 I would pass, because you give back every three-point Colts win. At +4 I would be more interested and might treat it as a real play rather than a lean.
